The Aquatic Plant Management (APM) program regulates the chemical, mechanical, physical,
and biological control of aquatic organisms in order to protect and develop diverse and stable
native aquatic plant communities.
ch. NR 107, Wis. Adm. Code, which regulates chemical control

ch. NR 109, Wis. Adm. Code, which regulates burning and mechanical, physical, and manual
control.

The program is currently regulated under two separate but
related administrative rules, ch. NR 107, Wis. Adm. Code, which regulates chemical control, and
ch. NR 109, Wis. Adm. Code, which regulates burning and mechanical, physical, and manual
control.

The proposed recreated ch. NR 107, Wis. Adm. Code, unifies all control activities under a
consistent set of procedures and policies that align with current state and federal law

improving
administrative consistency and efficiency as well as customer service.

global_field_review: A schema returns units only and forbids self-completeness. B returns mappings/bindings only and forbids whole-source completeness pronouncement. No raw global completeness claim to adopt. Runtime source_inventory_completeness, mapping_status, semantic_status and whole_record_fidelity remain unverified; action_ready/production_eligible false.

request_separation_and_exposure.stage_A: Full inspected request has exactly source_text and its binding in user data, with neutral source-only instructions/schema; no candidate record, candidate ID schedule, prior outputs or audit included.
request_separation_and_exposure.stage_B: Full inspected request has source, frozen A lossless tuple encoding, original-record operative projection and bindings; no original source-label/audit or R9 response included. Model receives neutral general failure-mode guidance in B, not WI expected answers.
request_separation_and_exposure.reviewer_exposure: Reviewer has seen the original source labels/audit, prior R8/R9 responses and known defects before this run, explicitly carried by preregistration. This is not clean blind review or human gold. Protocol design itself is informed by prior development failures; no causal attribution to staging alone.
